patients.summary: Healthy college student who joined at 18. Three mononucleosis-labeled throat illnesses in a year (practice 11/2024, ENT 5/2025 with amoxicillin rash, ED 11/2025), each recovering; otherwise routine prevention.

documents.title: Enrollment call
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Mother called on behalf of her son Eli (DOB 04/09/2005), who turned 18 this spring and is aging out of his pediatric office. Membership paperwork emailed to the patient; he signed it himself this afternoon. Booked new patient physical 6/20 at 8:40. Pediatric records release sent. Insurance: parent's employer plan, card scanned.

documents.title: New Patient Preventive Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
18 y/o young man here to establish adult primary care; coming from his pediatrician, records requested. No complaints today.

PMH: none. No surgeries. No hospitalizations.
Meds: none, no supplements.
Allergies: no known drug allergies.
Family: mother with hypothyroidism; father with hypertension. No autoimmune disease or blood cancers in the family that he knows of.
Social: lives with his parents in Haydenville. Student. Has never smoked or vaped, does not drink, no drug use. Wears a seat belt. Sleeps about 8 h.

ROS: negative across systems.

Exam: vitals in flowsheet. Well appearing, slim. HEENT: TMs clear, pharynx pink without tonsillar enlargement, no thyromegaly. No cervical or supraclavicular nodes. Heart regular rate and rhythm, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender, no organ enlargement. Skin clear. Neuro grossly intact. GU deferred.

Assessment/plan:
1. Adult wellness visit. Screening labs today: CBC, CMP, a one-time lipid panel, and one-time HIV and hep C screens, which he agreed to. PHQ-2 negative.
2. Immunizations: will reconcile against pediatric records once they arrive. Flu shot this fall.
3. Return yearly, or anytime by text or phone.

documents.title: Your lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Eli, everything from Tuesday is back and normal: blood count, kidney and liver tests, sugar, and cholesterol. The HIV and hepatitis C screens were negative too. Nothing to follow up on.

documents.title: Pediatric records received
documents.author: MA
documents.body:
Records received by fax from the patient's former pediatric office, 41 pages, scanned to media.

Summary for the chart: well-child visits yearly through age 17, growth along the 50th-75th percentile, no chronic problems, no surgeries, no medications, no drug allergies documented. Routine adolescent screening there was unremarkable.

Immunizations abstracted: full childhood series including MMR x2 and varicella x2; Tdap and MenACWY at 11; HPV 9-valent x2 (age 11, completed); MenACWY booster at 16; COVID-19 Pfizer primary series June 2021. Entered into the immunization record.

documents.title: Vaccine visit
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Here after school for fall vaccines. Screening questions negative, no prior reactions. Flu quadrivalent 0.5 mL IM left deltoid; Pfizer 2023-24 COVID 0.3 mL IM right deltoid. Waited 15 min, felt fine, left with VIS sheets.

documents.title: College forms
documents.author: patient
documents.body:
Hey, I'm starting college in the fall and living in the dorms. The school sent a health form that needs a physical within the last year and my shot record signed by a doctor. Can I come in sometime in July? I uploaded the form.
- Eli

documents.title: RE: College forms
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Hi Eli, you're booked for your physical Tuesday 7/23 at 10:00. Bring the form or we'll print the one you uploaded. The doctor will go over any vaccines the school asks about.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Eli is 19 and starting college this fall; he'll be in a freshman dorm. Feels well. Nothing new over the past year: no ED visits, no meds, still no drug allergies. Exercises by running a few times a week.

Social: no tobacco, nicotine or alcohol.
Family history unchanged (mother thyroid, father BP).

Exam: vitals reviewed, normal. Alert, healthy. Eyes, ears, throat normal. Neck supple, no adenopathy. Heart without murmur, lungs clear. Abdomen soft, no hepatosplenomegaly. Skin, extremities normal.

PHQ-9: 1.

Plan:
- College form completed: immunizations verified against records, MenACWY booster at 16 meets the dorm requirement.
- Talked through meningococcal B for a dorm-living college student; he wants it. Bexsero dose 1 today, dose 2 in a month or later.
- No labs needed this year; screening done last summer.
- Flu shot this fall, at school if easier, and let us know so we can record it.

documents.title: College form is ready
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Hi Eli, your college health form is signed and attached here as a PDF, with your immunization record. You'll need to upload both to the school's health portal yourself. Your second meningitis B shot can be done any time after 8/20; give us a call to set it up.

documents.title: MenB dose 2
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Second Bexsero today, 0.5 mL IM right deltoid. Dose 1 on 7/23 left him with an achy arm overnight, nothing else. Observed 15 minutes, no issues. Series complete. Moves into the dorm this weekend.

documents.title: Got my flu shot
documents.author: patient
documents.body: They had a flu clinic in the student center last week so I got it there on the 16th. Don't know which brand. Just letting you know for my record.

documents.title: RE: Got my flu shot
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Thanks Eli, added to your immunization history as given 10/16/2024 at the campus clinic.

documents.title: Triage: sore throat, fever
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Pt called, home from school for the holiday week. About a week of feeling run down, sore throat that is now making it hard to swallow, fevers, and his neck feels swollen. Swallowing liquids OK, no drooling, voice normal, breathing fine. No rash. Taking acetaminophen. Put on the doctor's schedule tomorrow 9:20. Told him to call back tonight or go to the ED if he can't keep fluids down or has trouble breathing.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Acute Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: 19 y/o college freshman, lives in a dorm, home this week. Roughly 7 days of illness. It started with a mild headache and tiredness and has steadily gotten worse: now feels wiped out, has fevers, and his throat hurts enough that swallowing is painful. Says his neck feels "puffy." No cough, no runny nose, no chest pain. No meds besides acetaminophen the last few days. NKDA. Never smoker, no alcohol.

O: T 38.5 C, other vitals as charted. Tired-looking but nontoxic, speaking full sentences, handling secretions. Tonsils enlarged with exudate bilaterally, uvula midline, no peritonsillar bulge. Prominent bilateral cervical lymphadenopathy. Lungs clear. Heart regular. Abdomen soft, spleen tip felt about 2 cm below the left costal margin, nontender; liver not enlarged. No rash.

Rapid strep in office: negative. CBC sent stat; peripheral smear reviewed with the lab shows atypical lymphocytes. Monospot sent.

A/P: Exudative pharyngitis with marked adenopathy, splenomegaly and atypical lymphocytes, strep negative. Infectious mononucleosis, pending heterophile.
- Supportive care: fluids, rest, acetaminophen or ibuprofen for throat pain and fever.
- No antibiotics.
- Spleen is enlarged: no contact sports, wrestling around, or heavy lifting for at least 4 weeks and until rechecked.
- Expect fatigue for a few weeks; okay to go back to classes as he feels able. Avoid sharing drinks.
- Recheck in about 3 weeks. Return sooner for trouble swallowing liquids, breathing difficulty, or left upper abdominal pain.

documents.title: Mono test result
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Eli, the mono test came back positive, which fits everything we saw Wednesday. Your white count is a little high with lots of reactive lymphocytes, also typical. Same plan: rest, fluids, pain relievers, and absolutely no contact sports or heavy lifting until I recheck your spleen. I put you on for 12/18.

documents.title: back at school
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Throat is way better and the fever is gone, still tired in the afternoons. I'm back on campus for finals. Can I go to the gym yet? Just treadmill, no lifting.

documents.title: RE: back at school
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Glad you're improving. Easy treadmill or walking is fine if you feel up to it. Still no weights and no pickup basketball or anything with contact until I've felt your belly. Keep the 12/18 visit, or if you're stuck on campus we can move it into January.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, low MDM

documents.title: Follow-up Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Missed the December slot during finals week, rescheduled for winter break.

Feeling normal again for about two weeks, energy back. No sore throat, no fevers. Has only done light cardio as told.

Afebrile, vitals fine. Throat clear, tonsils small, no exudate. Only a few small shotty cervical nodes. Abdomen soft, no splenomegaly palpable even on deep inspiration, liver normal.

A/P: Mononucleosis, recovered. CBC today to make sure counts have settled. Cleared to go back to the gym and normal activity, ramp up over a week or two.

documents.title: Blood count
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Your blood count from yesterday is completely normal now. Enjoy the rest of break.

medications.sig: Take 1 capsule by mouth three times daily for 10 days

documents.title: Fill history notice
documents.author: MA
documents.body: External fill feed: amoxicillin 500 mg capsules #30, 1 cap TID x 10 days, prescribed by an urgent care clinician, filled 5/17/2025. No record from the urgent care in the chart. Added to med list as an outside short course.

orders.reason: second exudative tonsillitis in six months

documents.title: rash
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Sore throat and feeling crappy for about a week, so I went to urgent care near school yesterday and they gave me amoxicillin. This morning I have a red blotchy rash all over my chest, back, arms and legs. Doesn't really itch. Throat still hurts and I'm exhausted. Should I keep taking it? I'm home now, semester ended Friday.

documents.title: RE: rash
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Stop the amoxicillin now and don't take any more. I'm marking amoxicillin as an allergy (rash) in your chart. If your lips, tongue or throat swell or you have any trouble breathing, call 911.

This is the second bad tonsil illness since November, so I'd like an ENT to look at your throat. They have an opening tomorrow morning and I've sent the referral; their office will call you. Tylenol or ibuprofen for the throat and fever, and plenty of fluids. Send me a message after you're seen.

documents.title: Check-in after ENT
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Called pt to follow up. Saw ENT Monday. Per pt, ENT told him this is mono again and said the rash was from the amoxicillin. No new prescriptions. Rash fading, throat a bit better, still low-grade temps and very tired. Swallowing OK. Reminded no contact sports or lifting until cleared. ENT note not received yet; will request.

documents.title: Records request
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Second request faxed to the ENT office for the 5/19 consult note. First request 5/22, nothing received. Spoke with their records line, they will send this week.

documents.title: Otolaryngology consultation, 05/19/2025
documents.author: otolaryngology
documents.body:
OTOLARYNGOLOGY — NEW CONSULTATION
Date of service: 05/19/2025
Referred by: primary care
Reason: sore throat, fatigue, rash after amoxicillin

HPI: 20-year-old male college student seen at the request of his primary care physician. One week of throat pain, fatigue and low-grade fever with poor appetite and general malaise. Started amoxicillin from an urgent care two days ago and since then has a diffuse red maculopapular eruption across the trunk and extremities. Of note he presented in November 2024 with malaise, sore throat, fever and neck swelling. He denies dyspnea and arthralgia.

Meds: amoxicillin (stopped by PCP 5/18).
Allergies: amoxicillin — maculopapular rash.
PMH: infectious mononucleosis 11/2024.
FH: mother hypothyroid, father hypertensive. No autoimmune disease or hematologic cancer.
SH: never smoker, no alcohol, college student living in residence hall.

Exam: Temp 38.4 C. Bilateral cervical lymphadenopathy. Tonsils enlarged with white exudates bilaterally, airway patent, no trismus, no peritonsillar fullness. Oral cavity otherwise normal. Ears and nose unremarkable. Lungs clear to auscultation; no cough, no wheeze. Maculopapular rash trunk and limbs.

Impression: Infectious mononucleosis, again, with the characteristic aminopenicillin rash.

Recommendations: supportive care with fluids, analgesics and rest. Avoid amoxicillin. No surgical intervention needed now. Return as needed.

— Otolaryngology

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
20 y/o here for yearly exam before heading back to school. Fully recovered from the May illness by early June. No throat trouble since. Working out normally. No meds.

Allergies: amoxicillin (rash, May 2025).
PMH: infectious mononucleosis 11/2024; ENT diagnosed mono again 5/2025 (letter in chart).
Social: college student, back in the dorm in a few weeks. No tobacco, vaping or alcohol.
FH unchanged.

Exam: vitals normal. Throat normal, tonsils not enlarged. No adenopathy. Heart and lungs normal. Abdomen soft, spleen and liver not palpable. Skin clear.

PHQ-9 2.

Plan:
- Mono resolved, off the active list. CBC and CMP today since he has had two of these illnesses.
- Immunizations current; flu and COVID in October.
- See him next summer, sooner as needed.

documents.title: Labs from your physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Eli, blood count and chemistry panel, including liver tests, are all normal. Have a good semester.

documents.title: Vaccines
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Home for fall break. Allergy to amoxicillin noted, no vaccine reactions. Trivalent flu 0.5 mL IM L deltoid, Moderna 2025-26 COVID 0.5 mL IM R deltoid. Observed 15 min, fine.

documents.title: ER yesterday
documents.author: patient
documents.body: I ended up in the ER yesterday. Throat has been killing me for like 10 days with fevers up to 102 and I could barely swallow. They did blood work and said it's mono AGAIN and my liver numbers are up a little. Sent me home. They said follow up with my doctor this week. I'm home until next week.

documents.title: RE: ER yesterday
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Sorry you're dealing with this again, Eli. The doctor can see you tomorrow, Tuesday, at 1:40. Please bring any paperwork the ER gave you. Until then fluids, rest, Tylenol or ibuprofen, and no sports or lifting.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: ED Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Seen in an outside ED Sunday 11/30 after about 10 days of fevers to 102, bad sore throat and painful swallowing, very fatigued. Brought the discharge sheet: diagnosis mononucleosis, mildly elevated liver enzymes, supportive care, follow up with PCP. Full ED record requested. Since Sunday throat a little better, eating soft foods, still tired. No rash this time, no cough or runny nose. No meds except ibuprofen.

PMH: mono 11/2024; mono per ENT 5/2025.
Allergies: amoxicillin (rash).

Exam: afebrile today, vitals as charted. Tonsils still enlarged with some residual exudate, oropharynx red. Anterior and posterior cervical nodes enlarged on both sides. Abdomen soft, spleen palpable just below the left costal margin, nontender; liver edge not felt.

A/P: Infectious mononucleosis per the ED, improving.
- Repeat CBC and liver panel today.
- Spleen enlarged again: no contact sports or lifting until rechecked, about a month.
- Supportive care. Avoid alcohol (doesn't drink anyway) while liver tests are up.
- Recheck after the holidays with labs.

documents.title: Yesterday's blood work
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Eli, your liver enzymes are already coming down (ALT 61, AST 47) and your blood count looks normal. That's the direction we want. We'll repeat them in early January when I see you.

documents.title: ED records request
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Request faxed to the hospital HIM department for the 11/30/2025 ED visit, notes and labs. Signed release on file.

documents.title: Emergency department record, 11/30/2025
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT PHYSICIAN NOTE
Arrival 11/30/2025 14:22

CC: fever, sore throat, odynophagia x 10 days.

HPI: 20M with prior episodes of infectious mononucleosis in November 2024 and May 2025 presents with recurrent upper respiratory illness. Began as mild throat discomfort and has progressed; now difficulty swallowing and profound fatigue. Tmax 38.9 C (102 F) at home. No cough, no rhinorrhea, no rash.

Meds: none. Allergies: amoxicillin (maculopapular rash).
FH: mother hypothyroidism; father HTN; no autoimmune or hematologic malignancy.
SH: college student in dormitory. Never smoker. No EtOH.

Exam: Bilateral anterior and posterior cervical lymphadenopathy. Oropharynx erythematous, tonsils enlarged with exudate, uvula midline, tolerating secretions. Spleen palpable 2 cm below the left costal margin. No hepatomegaly. Remainder of exam unremarkable.

Labs: WBC 12.0 K/uL (ref 4.5-11.0); atypical lymphocytes 20%; ALT 70 U/L (ref 7-56); AST 65 U/L (ref 8-48).

MDM/Impression: Infectious mononucleosis, third episode by history, with mild transaminase elevation and splenomegaly. Airway not threatened, tolerating PO.

Disposition: discharged home. Supportive care, hydration, acetaminophen or ibuprofen. No contact sports. Follow up with PCP this week.

— Emergency Medicine

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, low MDM

documents.title: Follow-up Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Back to baseline since mid-December. Eating normally, no fevers, energy good. ED record from 11/30 now in the chart and reviewed (WBC 12.0, atypicals 20%, ALT 70, AST 65).

Vitals normal. Pharynx clear, tonsils no longer enlarged. No significant adenopathy. Abdomen soft, no splenomegaly. Liver not enlarged.

A/P: Mononucleosis episode resolved. CBC and liver panel today; if normal he is cleared for all activity including sports when he returns to campus.

documents.title: All clear
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Liver tests are normal now (ALT 29, AST 24) and so is your blood count. You're cleared for everything, sports included.

documents.title: shot record
documents.author: patient
documents.body: School wants an updated copy of my immunizations with the newer flu and covid ones on it. Can you post it on here?

documents.title: RE: shot record
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Hi Eli, your full immunization record is attached as a PDF, current through the 10/14/2025 flu and COVID doses.

documents.title: Insurance card
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Mother called, new member ID card from her employer plan as of 6/1, same carrier. Pt emailed a photo of the card; updated in registration.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
21 y/o, yearly visit, school form for the fall. No illnesses since the January visit, no throat infections. Running and lifting without problems. No meds.

Allergies: amoxicillin (rash).
Hx: mononucleosis episodes 11/2024, 5/2025 (ENT) and 11/2025 (ED), each resolved.
Social: college student, living in the dorm again this fall. No nicotine, no alcohol.
FH: mother hypothyroidism, father HTN.

Exam: vitals normal. HEENT normal, tonsils small. No lymphadenopathy. Cardiopulmonary normal. Abdomen without organomegaly. Skin normal.

PHQ-2 0.

Plan: healthy. No labs this year. School form completed. Flu vaccine in October; booked. Return next summer.
